headline: Every cell in your body was built from food you ate—you literally are what you eat
universal_truth: Inputs become outputs; what you take in shapes what you become
fun_facts: Your body replaces most cells every 7-10 years—the material comes from food
The atoms in your body right now were once in other living things—and will be again
Digestion breaks food down to molecular building blocks, which your body reassembles into you
discussion_questions: How does knowing food becomes you change how you think about eating?
What else do you 'consume' that becomes part of you?
How does the quality of inputs affect the quality of outputs?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The cells in your body are built from food you ate. That apple, that sandwich, that salad—their molecules were disassembled and reassembled into you. You are literally constructed from what you consume. 'You are what you eat' isn't metaphor—it's biology.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Food seems to disappear when we eat it. But where does it actually go? How does a meal become muscle, bone, and brain?

options.text: Digestion breaks food into molecular components that are absorbed and rebuilt into body structures
options.response: Yes. Your digestive system is a disassembly line; your cells are the rebuild crew. Proteins become your proteins. Fats become your fats. You're constantly rebuilding yourself from raw materials.

options.text: Food provides energy that powers body processes
options.response: Energy is one use, but food also provides the physical building materials that become your body...

q1.title: Molecular Lego
q1.script: Digestion breaks food into basic molecules: amino acids, fatty acids, sugars. These are absorbed into your blood and distributed to cells. Your cells then reassemble these blocks into new proteins, membranes, and structures. Same blocks, new you.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Molecular Lego"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Constant Renewal
q2.script: Your body replaces most of its cells over 7-10 years. Skin cells last weeks, red blood cells months, bone cells years. The material for every replacement comes from food. You're constantly rebuilding yourself from what you eat.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Atoms Cycle
q3.script: The atoms in your body were once in other living things—plants, animals, ancient organisms. After you, they'll become part of something else. You're a temporary arrangement of atoms borrowed from the world and recycled through food.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Inputs become outputs. What you take in shapes what you become—literally, with food. This applies beyond nutrition: what you read, watch, and think also shapes who you are. Choose your inputs wisely.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 130. Tomorrow, we continue exploring cultures and human achievement. Until then, at your next meal, consider that those molecules will become part of you.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Input Awareness - Choose What Becomes You
growTrack.learning_objective: Connect inputs to their effects on who you become
growTrack.activity: At your next meal, consider: these molecules will be disassembled and rebuilt into my body. Does that change what you want to eat? Then expand the thought: what other 'inputs'—information, media, relationships—are shaping who you become?
